stage: One np bridge start per session when a command arrives during startup (desktop first message); race-free bridge state and manifests
scope: The np mod bridge start (launch single-flight, failed-start, doctor-restore and exit state writes judged inside the updater, exits matched by a per-launch id), /np doctor reporting from the live connection, per-process bridge manifests released on close, and removal of compiled JavaScript committed beside the mod sources. The desktop app run (AC9) needs the person after install.

finding.observed: Desktop check: the first message /np doctor started the session while activation started bridge A; the command started bridge B; both chose socket b-c4a99405a223.sock, B failed BRIDGE_RUNNING, deleted A's manifest and overwrote the state to down while A (pid 57570) stayed connected.
finding.evidence: desktop session 6ef2bbab transcript; live listener on the session socket with no manifest; zero-API reproduction (two starts, bridge down) with the pre-fix mod

full_suite.note: Run on the branch merged with main 4146b47. The identical failure set, by test id, as the run before the merge and the merged desktop-host run: failures shared with main plus the two evidence-pointer checks this publication regenerates.

startup_race_harness.control: The same run on the pre-fix mod (f3bcc2e): starts 2, doctor bridge: down (A bridge already serves this Claude session).

operation_checks.parent_context: disposable interactive claude 2.1.314 in a temporary HOME with the np mod loaded by --plugin-dir; replay bridge behind a wrapper npeer that waits 3 s; no model input
operation_checks.scope: /np doctor typed while activation's bridge start is in flight: one bridge start, doctor reports bridge: ready, no tripwire hit. The pre-fix mod (f3bcc2e) under the same run: two starts, bridge down with BRIDGE_RUNNING.

limitations: The desktop app run (AC9) is verified only by the person after install.
The desktop composer shows "/np isn't a command here." for /np; the command still runs.
A desktop session whose state already reads down from the pre-fix mod stays down until a new session starts on the installed fix.

independent_review.reviewer: codex gpt-6.1-sol xhigh, NativePeers analysis workers (read-only)
independent_review.note: Reviewers read source and reproduced interleavings against the documented $.state read/compare/retry behaviour; they ran no test suite.

findings.summary: The startup guard was checked before an unprotected session-id await, so activation and /np doctor could both start a bridge.
findings.disposition: FIXED in 50a06a0: launch() takes the single start slot synchronously before its first await; callers wait for an in-flight start through $ calls.

findings.summary: A failed start could overwrite a connected bridge's state with down after its connection check went stale.
findings.disposition: FIXED in 50a06a0 and 1c08cf9: the failed-start updater keeps a ready state.

findings.summary: Doctor could restore ready after the bridge had exited.
findings.disposition: FIXED in 1c08cf9: liveness and generation are judged inside the updater on every retry.

findings.summary: Pre-existing: shutdown cleanup could unlink a successor's manifest recorded at the same path while close() drained an in-flight spawn.
findings.disposition: FIXED in 1c08cf9 after a compare-before-unlink in 50a06a0 left a window: each bridge process keeps its own manifest file and releases only that file.

findings.summary: Doctor's restore checked liveness before update(), which reads, compares and retries.
findings.disposition: FIXED in 1c08cf9 (bridgeRestored takes a live predicate evaluated inside the updater).

findings.summary: Module-local guards let a hot-reload predecessor overwrite its successor's state.
findings.disposition: FIXED in 1c08cf9 (rules judged on the shared state inside the updater) and ff2bbfd (exit matched by launch id).

findings.summary: The manifest compare-then-unlink left a window between the read and the unlink across processes.
findings.disposition: FIXED in 1c08cf9: manifest file per process id, so release never reads another process's record.

findings.summary: An accepted late rebind could overwrite or recreate a successor's manifest record.
findings.disposition: FIXED in 1c08cf9: no record once released; each process writes only its own path.

rounds.result: All four previous P2 findings resolved; no new defect introduced.

findings.summary: Pre-existing in f3bcc2e: a predecessor's exit matched by a reused socket path could mark a live successor down (SIGTERM drain during a hot reload).
findings.disposition: FIXED in ff2bbfd: each launch stores a nonsecret random id in the shared state; the exit updater compares that id.

rounds.result: Resolved: a predecessor's exit after socket reuse, in both the reload overlap and the SIGTERM drain; no shared-state ownership check still uses the socket or a module-local generation; the launch id reaches only session $.state and the bearer token stays out of it. No new defect.
